headline: Phantom Vault Ring Cracked — Stolen Data Spanned Six Corporate Networks
body:
Meridian 88 authorities confirmed today that a coordinated data theft operation known internally as Phantom Vault had been systematically extracting proprietary information from at least six corponation networks since 2109, representing what one Federal Remnant cybercrime analyst called 'the largest sustained cross-border data exfiltration in the city's history.' Among the confirmed victims: Axiom, Helix Biosystems, Sterling-Nakamura, Palladian, Zheng-Dao, and Ferrogate Transit. The stolen material reportedly includes pharmaceutical synthesis protocols, personnel blackmail files, transit infrastructure schematics, and three years of Sterling-Nakamura internal financial communications.

The ring operated through a layered network of physical and digital couriers — using human runners carrying air-gapped data chips through The Underworld tunnel network to avoid corporate packet-sniffing on surface-level data lines. Arrests made this week include seventeen individuals across The Narrows, Geartown, and The Circuit, but investigators say the operation's architects remain unidentified. 'The people we arrested are the hands,' said Deputy Marshal Coran Whitfield-Naidu at this morning's press briefing. 'We have not found the brain.' Leaked arrest documents suggest several of the detained were themselves unaware they were part of a larger operation, having accepted individual courier contracts through standard runner brokerage channels.

The Graycloaks have issued a rare public statement denying involvement and calling the suggestion 'irresponsible.' Iron Lotus has said nothing, which investigators note is the organization's standard response to questions about operations it ran. The stolen Helix Biosystems data is of particular concern — it reportedly includes early-stage SNT research files that had not yet been disclosed publicly, raising questions about whether a competitor corponation commissioned the theft or whether Phantom Vault was selling to the highest bidder on open grey markets.
aftermath: Three months after the arrests, a partial Helix Biosystems SNT research file appeared for sale through a Bore Rats-connected data broker in The Underworld, suggesting Phantom Vault's data inventory had been partially distributed before the ring was disrupted.
runner_relevance: Phantom Vault's exposure created cascading contract demand across the runner economy. Corponations immediately hired runners for counter-intelligence sweeps — attempting to trace which of their active contractors had unknowingly participated in the ring. Simultaneously, Iron Lotus and competing data brokers put out acquisition contracts for the remaining Phantom Vault data inventory before Federal Remnant could seize it. Runners with clean records and no known affiliation suddenly commanded premium rates for sensitive courier work as every corponation re-evaluated its supply chain. The Helix SNT file specifically generated a long-running series of retrieval and counter-retrieval contracts that persisted for years.
